Security Alert: U.S. Embassy Jerusalem – October 25, 2026

Security Alert: U.S. Embassy Jerusalem – October 25, 2026

U.S. Embassy Jerusalem has been informed that all settlements in the West Bank are closed to Palestinian workers October 25 and 26, 2026 with the exception of industrial zones and a limited number of other approved areas. Additionally, checkpoints will be closed October 27, 2026, across the entire West Bank region in connection with the Israeli election.  This means that there will be no regular entry into Israel or into settlements in the West Bank.

More information will be shared if there are any significant changes to this policy. This is provided for your information as you make your own security plans.

Actions to Take:

  • Refer to our website for the latest Security Alerts: https://il.usembassy.gov/category/alert/. 
  • Be aware of your surroundings. 
  • Learn the location of the nearest bomb shelter or other hardened shelter. Download the Home Front Command Red Alert application or similar apps for mobile devices (available on devices within Israel) to receive real time alerts for rocket and missile attacks and armed UAV intrusions. 
  • Avoid all demonstrations and large gatherings. 
  • Avoid all areas where there is a heavy police presence. 
  • Monitor local media. 
  • Follow the instructions of local authorities. 
  • Enroll in the Department of State’s Smart Traveler Enrollment Program (STEP). STEP enrollment gives you the latest security updates and makes it easier for the U.S. Embassy to contact you in an emergency. 
  • Regularly monitor the State Department’s website, where you can find current Travel Advisories (including the Travel Advisory for Israel, the West Bank, and Gaza) and the Worldwide Caution. Read the Country Information for Israel, the West Bank, and Gaza. For additional information, refer to “Traveler’s Checklist” on the State Department’s website.

Security Alert: U.S. Embassy Jerusalem – October 23, 2026

Security Alert: U.S. Embassy Jerusalem – October 23, 2026

The Travel Advisory for Israel was updated on October 23, 2026, to reflect the threat of increased Iranian-supported Houthi regional aggression. The Travel Advisory reads:

There were no changes to the advisory level or risk indicators. Advisory summary was updated to reflect an increase in potential armed attacks by the Iranian-supported Houthis and Iranian efforts to target U.S. government officials in the region.

Reconsider Travel to Israel due to terrorism and unrest. Some areas have increased risk. Read the entire Travel Advisory.

  • Do Not Travel to areas north of Route 85 to Route 90 (south) to Route 87 due to armed conflict.
  • Do Not Travel within 11.3 kilometers/7 miles of the Gaza Strip due to armed conflict.
  • Do Not Travel within 2.4 kilometers/1.5 miles of the Israel-Egypt border, except at the area of the Taba border crossing, also known as the Menachem Begin crossing, due to armed conflict.  

Advisory summary

As of August 26, 2026, family members may join U.S. government employees who work in Israel.

U.S. government employee travel restrictions U.S. government employees working in Israel are restricted from the following locations due to safety risks:

  • Areas north of Route 85 to Route 90 (south) to Route 87; 
  • Within 11.3 kilometers/7 miles of the Gaza Strip; and
  • Within 2.4 kilometers/1.5 miles of the Israel-Egypt border, except at the area of the Taba border crossing, also known as the Menachem Begin crossing.

Any official travel of U.S. government personnel within these areas requires approval from the U.S. embassy’s security office. Additional staffing posture adjustments may be imposed on U.S. personnel under Chief of Mission security responsibility due to evolving security issues.

Armed Conflict

Iranian-supported Houthis have engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure resulting in civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions. The hostilities have the potential to escalate rapidly beyond that immediate area.

Terrorism

There is risk of terrorist violence, including terrorist attacks and other activity in Israel.  Visit the U.S. Department of State’s country reports on terrorism to learn more.

Unrest

The security environment in Israel is complex and can change quickly. Violence can occur without warning.  Increased regional tensions can cause airlines to cancel or limit flights into and out of Israel.

Risks in specific areas

Level 4 – Do Not Travel

Areas north of Route 85 to Route 90 (south) to Route 87

Do Not Travel to areas north of Route 85 to Route 90 (south) to Route 87 due to armed conflict. 

The Israeli authorities restrict travel to areas north of Route 85 to Route 90 (south) to Route 87 due to Israeli Defense Forces presence and activity. Do not travel to this area for any reason.

U.S. government employees working in Israel are not allowed to travel to areas north of Route 85 to Route 90 (south) to Route 87. Any official travel of U.S. government personnel within these areas requires approval from the U.S. embassy’s security office.

Within 11.3 kilometers/7 miles of the Gaza Strip

Do Not Travel within 11.3 kilometers/7 miles of the Gaza Strip due to armed conflict.

Within 2.4 kilometers/1.5 miles of the Israel-Egypt border

Do Not Travel within 2.4 kilometers/1.5 miles of the Israel-Egypt border, except at the area of the Taba border crossing, also known as the Menachem Begin crossing, due to armed conflict.

If you decide to travel to Israel:

  • Enroll in the Smart Traveler Enrollment Program (STEP) to receive important updates and alerts from the U.S. embassy or consulate.   Enrolling helps the U.S. embassy or consulate contact you or your emergency contact in an emergency.
  • Review the Country Security Report for Israel.
  • Review our information on Terrorism and Travel to High-Risk Areas.
  • Maintain a high degree of situational awareness and always exercise caution, especially at checkpoints and other areas with a significant presence of security forces.
  • Beware of and report suspicious activities, including unattended items, to local police.
  • Avoid demonstrations and crowds.
  • Have a plan to leave in an emergency that does not depend on U.S. government help.  Review our information on Crisis and Evacuations.
  • Follow the instructions of security and emergency response officials.
  • Learn the location of the nearest bomb shelter or other hardened shelter.
  • Download the Home Front Command Red Alert application or similar apps for mobile devices (available on devices within Israel) to receive real time alerts for rocket and missile attacks and armed UAV intrusions.  U.S. government employees in Israel are encouraged to use these apps.
  • When traveling in rural areas, exercise caution due to the possibility of unexploded ordnance.
  • Visit the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) website for the latest Travel Health Information for Israel. 
  • Whether you’re a first time or frequent traveler, use the International Travel Checklist.
  • We highly recommend that you buy travel insurance before you travel.  Check with your travel insurance provider about evacuation assistance, medical insurance, and trip cancelation coverage.

Security Alert: U.S. Embassy Jerusalem – October 13, 2026


Event: Unexploded ordnance and other explosive weapons remain a risk throughout Israel, the West Bank and Gaza, especially in the vicinity of borders. The locations of unexploded ordnance are often not marked or easy to recognize. Rain, flooding, farming, and construction often bring buried ordnance to the surface making them more unstable.

Unexploded ordnance comes in many shapes and sizes and may be rusted, partly buried, or hard to recognize. Examples of unexploded ordnance include artillery shells, mortar rounds, rockets, grenades, small round “bomblet” cluster submunitions (which may look like balls or toys), landmines, fuses and metal cylinders. Assume all unidentified objects are dangerous.

Follow the “3 Rs”: Recognize, Retreat, Report

  1. RECOGNIZE. Stop moving when you see a suspicious object. Do not go closer to get a better look.
  2. RETREAT. Move away carefully the same way you came in. Keep others, especially children, away from the area.
  3. REPORT. Once you are a safe distance away, contact Israeli National Police’s emergency phone number at 100.

Do NOT

  • Do not go near or make physical contact with any suspected unexploded ordnance.
  • Do not throw objects at it to mark it or to try to set it off.
  • Do not use radios or mobile phones right next to the item. Move far away first.
  • Do not collect, buy, or keep ordnance, shell casings, or “war souvenirs,” even ones described as inert or deactivated. 

Actions:

  • Do not go into areas marked with unexploded ordnance or landmine warning signs.

                                             

  • Stay on paved roads and well-used paths when you travel outside urban areas.
  • Talk with your children about unexploded ordnance. Teach them never to touch strange metal objects and immediately inform an adult should they encounter one.
  • Learn the location of the nearest bomb shelter or other hardened shelter. Download the Home Front Command Red Alert application or similar apps for mobile devices (available on devices within Israel) to receive real time alerts for rocket and missile attacks and armed UAV intrusions. 
  • Enroll in the Department of State’s Smart Traveler Enrollment Program (STEP). STEP enrollment gives you the latest security updates and makes it easier for the U.S. Embassy to contact you in an emergency. 
  • Regularly monitor the State Department’s website, where you can find current Travel Advisories (including the Travel Advisory for Israel, the West Bank, and Gaza) and the Worldwide Caution. For additional information, refer to “Traveler’s Checklist” on the State Department’s website.

Security Alert: U.S. Embassy Jerusalem – October 8, 2026

Event: Americans currently in the Middle East should exercise heightened vigilance due to the complex security environment. Be aware of potential flight cancellations, airspace closures, and travel disruptions.

Check your flight’s departure status with the airline directly or through:

  • Tel Aviv: https://www.iaa.gov.il/en/airports/ben-gurion/flight-board
  • Haifa: https://www.iaa.gov.il/en/airports/haifa/flight-board/?flightType=departures

Iranian-supported Houthis have engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure resulting in civilian casualties. The hostilities have the potential to escalate rapidly.

Americans traveling to or from the Middle East should monitor information about airport and airline operations.

Iran and groups supportive of Iran may target other U.S. interests overseas or at locations associated with the United States and Americans throughout the world, including U.S. businesses and other institutions.

Operating Status:

The U.S. Embassy Jerusalem and Embassy Branch Office Tel Aviv consular sections are open for routine and emergency consular services.

Actions to Take:

  • Enroll in the Department of States Smart Traveler Enrollment Program (STEP). STEP enrollment gives you the latest security updates and makes it easier for the U.S. embassy to contact you in an emergency.
  • Know the location of your closest shelter or protected space.
  • Download the free Israel Defense Forces Home Front Command application on Android or Apple devices to receive real-time alerts for rockets, missile attacks, and armed UAV intrusions. Free commercial applications, such as â€œRed Alert: Israel,â€ are also available.
  • Find a secure location within your residence or another safe building. Have a supply of food, water, medications, and other essential items.
  • If an aerial attack occurs, stay away from glass doors, windows, and any fallen debris, and monitor your phone and news outlets for official guidance.
  • Keep your cell phone charged and pre-programmed with the emergency numbers listed below.
  • Be aware of your surroundings.
  • Avoid all demonstrations and large gatherings.
  • Avoid all areas where there is a heavy police presence.
  • Monitor local media.
  • Follow the instructions of local authorities.
  • Contact your airline directly for flight change details if your flight is affected.
  • Exercise caution and stay alert at locations publicly associated with the United States.
  • Keep a low profile.

Assistance: 

  • Israel Police: call 100
  • Israel Ambulance: call 101
  • U.S. Embassy Jerusalem: JerusalemACS@state.gov
  • U.S. Embassy Branch Office Tel Aviv: TelAvivACS@state.gov
  • U.S. Department of State Consular Affairs Call Center: +1-202-501-4444 (from abroad) or 1-888-407-4747 (from U.S./Canada).

U.S. Embassy Jerusalem has been informed that checkpoints will be closed October 5, 2026 and October 7, 2026, across the entire West Bank region.  This means that there is no regular entry into Israel except for strictly medical and humanitarian reasons.

Subject: Security Alert: U.S. Embassy Jerusalem – September 19, 2026

Event: Due to tensions in the Middle East, the security environment remains complex with the potential for unforeseen escalation.

Americans currently in the Middle East should exercise heightened vigilance and be aware of potential flight cancellations, airspace closures, and travel disruptions.

 Check your flight’s departure status with the airline directly or through:

  • Tel Aviv: https://www.iaa.gov.il/en/airports/ben-gurion/flight-board
  • Haifa: https://www.iaa.gov.il/en/airports/haifa/flight-board/?flightType=departures

Iranian-supported Houthis have engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including civilian airports. This military conflict has the potential to escalate rapidly.

Americans traveling to or from the region should monitor information about airport and airline operations.

U.S. diplomatic facilities, including outside the Middle East, have been targeted. Iran and groups supportive of Iran may target other U.S. interests overseas or at locations associated with the United States and Americans throughout the world, including U.S. businesses and other institutions.

Operating Status

The U.S. Embassy Jerusalem and Embassy Branch Office Tel Aviv consular sections are both open for routine and emergency consular services.

Actions to Take:

  • Enroll in the Department of State’s Smart Traveler Enrollment Program (STEP). STEP enrollment gives you the latest security updates and makes it easier for the U.S. embassy to contact you in an emergency.
  • Know the location of your closest shelter or protected space.
  • Download the free Israel Defense Forces Home Front Command application on Android or Apple devices to receive real-time alerts for rockets, missile attacks, and armed UAV intrusions. Free commercial applications, such as Red Alert: Israel are also available.
  • Find a secure location within your residence or another safe building.  Have a supply of food, water, medications, and other essential items.
  • If an aerial attack occurs, stay away from glass doors, windows, and any fallen debris, and monitor your phone and news outlets for official guidance.
  • Keep your cell phone charged and pre-programmed with the emergency numbers listed below.
  • Be aware of your surroundings.
  • Avoid all demonstrations and large gatherings.
  • Avoid all areas where there is a heavy police presence.
  • Monitor local media.
  • Follow the instructions of local authorities.
  • Contact your airline directly for flight change details if your flight is affected.
  • Exercise caution and stay alert at locations publicly associated with the United States.
  • Keep a low profile.

Assistance:

  • Israel Police:  call 100
  • Israel Ambulance:  call 101
  • U.S. Embassy Jerusalem:  JerusalemACS@state.gov
  • U.S. Embassy Branch Office Tel Aviv:  TelAvivACS@state.gov
  • U.S. Department of State Consular Affairs Call Center: +1-202-501-4444 (from abroad) or +1-888-407-4747 (from U.S./Canada).

  • Download the free Israel Defense Forces Home Front Command application onAndroid or Apple devices to receive real-time alerts for rockets, missile attacks, and armed UAV intrusions.  Free commercial applications, such as “Red Alert: Israel,” are also available.
  • Find a secure location within your residence or another safe building. Have a supply of food, water, medications, and other essential items.

  • If an aerial attack occurs, stay away from glass doors, windows, and any fallen debris, and monitor your phone and news outlets for official guidance.

  • Keep your cell phone charged and pre-programmed with the emergency numbers listed below.
  • Be aware of your surroundings. 
  • Avoid all demonstrations and large gatherings.
  • Avoid all areas where there is a heavy police presence.
  • Monitor local media.
  • Follow the instructions of local authorities.
  • Contact your airline directly for flight change details if your flight is affected.
  • Exercise caution and stay alert at locations publicly associated with the United States.
  • Keep a low profile.

Travel Advisory: Israel, the West Bank and Gaza (August 26, 2026)

 

The Department of State renewed its Travel Advisory  for Israel on August 26, 2026.  There were no changes to the Travel Advisory Level.  Advisory summary was updated to reflect that family members may travel to Israel.

Reconsider Travel to Israel due to terrorism and unrest. Some areas have increased risk. Read the entire Travel Advisory.

  • Do Not Travel to areas north of Route 85 to Route 90 (south) to Route 87 due to armed conflict.
  • Do Not Travel within 11.3 kilometers/7 miles of the Gaza Strip due to armed conflict.
  • Do Not Travel within 2.4 kilometers/1.5 miles of the Israel-Egypt border, except at the area of the Taba border crossing, also known as the Menachem Begin crossing, due to armed conflict.

Advisory summary

As of August 26, 2026, family members may join U.S. government employees who work in Israel.

U.S. government employee travel restrictions

U.S. government employees working in Israel are restricted from the following locations due to safety risks:

  • Areas north of Route 85 to Route 90 (south) to Route 87;
  • Within 11.3 kilometers/7 miles of the Gaza Strip; and
  • Within 2.4 kilometers/1.5 miles of the Israel-Egypt border, except at the area of the Taba border crossing, also known as the Menachem Begin crossing.

Any official travel of U.S. government personnel within these areas requires approval from the U.S. embassy’s security office.

Additional movement restrictions may be imposed on U.S. government employees working in Israel, with little to no notice, due to increased security issues or threats.

Terrorism

There is risk of terrorist violence, including terrorist attacks and other activity in Israel. Visit the U.S. Department of State’s country reports on terrorism to learn more.

Unrest

The security environment in Israel is complex and can change quickly. Violence can occur without warning. Increased regional tensions can cause airlines to cancel or limit flights into and out of Israel.

Risks in specific areas

Level 4 – Do Not Travel

Areas north of Route 85 to Route 90 (south) to Route 87

Do Not Travel to areas north of Route 85 to Route 90 (south) to Route 87 due to armed conflict.

The Israeli authorities restrict travel to areas north of Route 85 to Route 90 (south) to Route 87 due to Israeli Defense Forces presence and activity. Do not travel to this area for any reason.

U.S. government employees working in Israel are not allowed to travel to areas north of Route 85 to Route 90 (south) to Route 87. Any official travel of U.S. government personnel within these areas requires approval from the U.S. embassy’s security office.

Within 11.3 kilometers/7 miles of the Gaza Strip

Do Not Travel within 11.3 kilometers/7 miles of the Gaza Strip due to armed conflict.

Within 2.4 kilometers/1.5 miles of the Israel-Egypt border

Do Not Travel within 2.4 kilometers/1.5 miles of the Israel-Egypt border, except at the area of the Taba border crossing, also known as the Menachem Begin crossing, due to armed conflict.

If you decide to travel to Israel:

  • Enroll in the Smart Traveler Enrollment Program (STEP) to get important updates and alerts from the U.S. embassy or consulate. Enrolling helps the U.S. embassy or consulate contact you or your emergency contact in an emergency.
  • Review the Country Security Report for Israel.
  • Review our information on Terrorism and Travel to High-Risk Areas.
  • Maintain a high degree of situational awareness and always exercise caution, especially at checkpoints and other areas with a significant presence of security forces.
  • Beware of and report suspicious activities, including unattended items, to local police.
  • Avoid demonstrations and crowds.
  • Have a plan to leave in an emergency that does not depend on U.S. government help. Review our information on Crisis and Evacuations.
  • Follow the instructions of security and emergency response officials.
  • Learn the location of the nearest bomb shelter or other hardened shelter.
  • Download the Home Front Command Red Alert application or similar apps for mobile devices (available on devices within Israel) to receive real time alerts for rocket and missile attacks and armed UAV intrusions. U.S. government employees in Israel are encouraged to use these apps.
  • When traveling in rural areas, exercise caution due to the possibility of unexploded ordnance.
  • Visit the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) website for the latest Travel Health Information for Israel.
  • Whether you’re a first time or frequent traveler, use the International Travel Checklist.
  • We highly recommend that you buy travel insurance before you travel. Check with your travel insurance provider about evacuation assistance, medical insurance, and trip cancelation coverage.

TRAVEL ADVISORY – West Bank

Level 3 – Reconsider Travel

T – Terrorism

U – Unrest

Reconsider Travel to West Bank due to terrorism and unrest.

 

Advisory summary

 

U.S. government employee travel restrictions 

 

U.S. government employees working in Israel must obtain special authorization for official travel to the West Bank due to safety risks.

U.S. government employees working in Israel and their family members are currently restricted from all personal travel to the West Bank, except:

  • Travel on Routes 1, 90 (to the Allenby Bridge crossing), and 443 at any time.
  • Travel to Jericho and Bethlehem, including Beit Jala and Beit Sahour from dawn to midnight.
    • Checkpoint 300 near Rachel’s Tomb is the only permitted and accessible route into Bethlehem for U.S. government employees and their family members.  This is due to continued closures of checkpoints throughout the West Bank.

Due to increased security threats, additional movement restrictions may be imposed on U.S. government employees working in Israel, with little to no notice.

Terrorism

During the last year, there has been an increase in terrorist attacks in the West Bank.

There is a risk of terrorist violence, including terrorist attacks and other activity in West Bank.  Visit the U.S. Department of State’s country reports on terrorism to learn more.

Unrest

During the last year, there has been an increase in violence and Israeli military operations in the West Bank.  Some incidents have resulted in injury or the death of U.S. citizens.

During periods of unrest, the Israeli government may restrict access to and within the West Bank. Some areas may be placed under curfew.

If you decide to travel to the West Bank:

·        Enroll in the Smart Traveler Enrollment Program (STEP) to get important updates and alerts from the U.S. embassy or consulate.  Enrolling helps the U.S. embassy or consulate contact you or your emergency contact in an emergency.

·        Review the Country Security Report for Israel, West Bank and Gaza.

·        Review our information on Terrorism and Travel to High-Risk Areas.

·        Maintain a high degree of situational awareness and exercise caution, especially at checkpoints and other areas with a significant presence of security forces.

·        Beware of and report suspicious activities, including unattended items, to local police.

·        Avoid demonstrations and crowds.

·        Have a plan to leave in an emergency that does not depend on U.S. government help. Review our information on Crisis and Evacuations.

·        Follow the instructions of security and emergency response officials.

·        Learn the location of the nearest bomb shelter or other hardened shelter.

·        Download the Home Front Command Red Alert application or similar apps for mobile devices (available on devices within Israel) to receive real time alerts for rocket and missile attacks and armed UAV intrusions.  U.S. government employees in Israel are encouraged to use these apps.

·        When traveling in rural areas, exercise caution due to the possibility of unexploded ordnance.

·        Visit the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) website for the latest Travel Health Information for Israel.

·        Whether you’re a first time or frequent traveler, use the International Travel Checklist.

·        We highly recommend that you buy travel insurance before you travel.  Check with your travel insurance provider about evacuation assistance, medical insurance, and trip cancelation coverage.

 

TRAVEL ADVISORY – Gaza

Level 4 – Do Not Travel

T – Terrorism

U – Unrest

H – Health

Do Not Travel to Gaza due to terrorism, unrest, and limited health infrastructure.

Advisory Summary:

Restrictions on U.S. Government Personnel Movement

U.S. government employees are prohibited from traveling to Gaza for any reason due to safety risks. The U.S. government is unable to provide routine or emergency consular services to U.S. citizens in Gaza.

Terrorism

Terrorist groups, lone-actor terrorists, and other violent extremists continue plotting possible attacks in Gaza.  Terrorists and violent extremists may attack with little or no warning, targeting tourist locations, transportation hubs, markets, shopping malls, and local government facilities.  The security environment is complex and can change quickly.

There is risk of terrorist violence, including terrorist attacks and other activity in Gaza. Visit the U.S. Department of State’s country reports on terrorism to learn more.

Unrest

The security environment within Gaza and on its borders is extremely dangerous and volatile.

If you are a U.S. citizen or Lawful Permanent Resident (LPR) who needs our assistance, and you have not already provided your information to the Department of State, please email U.S. Embassy Jerusalem at JerusalemACS@state.gov.

Health

Emergency and intensive care facilities are limited in Gaza. Hospitals and clinics lack basic resources.

For U.S. citizens in Gaza:

  • Enroll in the Smart Traveler Enrollment Program (STEP) to get important updates and alerts from the U.S. embassy or consulate.  Enrolling helps the U.S. embassy or consulate contact you or your emergency contact in an emergency.
  • Review the Country Security Report for Israel, West Bank, and Gaza.
  • Review our information on Terrorism and Travel to High-Risk Areas.
  • Be prepared for an indefinite stay as the crossings between Gaza with Israel and Egypt can close without advance notice and for long periods during times of unrest and armed conflict. This includes having food, supplies, and medicine for an extended or indefinite period.
  • Have a plan to leave in an emergency that does not depend on U.S. government help.  Review our information on Crisis and Evacuations.
  • Maintain a high degree of situational awareness and always exercise caution, especially at checkpoints and other areas with a significant presence of security forces.
  • Avoid demonstrations and crowds.
  • If you use assistive or medical devices that require a power supply, be sure to find backup power or other ways that will sustain your device or equipment without access to power.
  • Make sure your insurance includes medical evacuation coverage.
  • Check with your doctor about required vaccines and shots for high-risk exposure before you go to Gaza.  Review the Health section in the Travel Guidance for Gaza.
